briefing.summary: Dive to a dense cluster within the Blake Plateau coral mound province. Survey the raised mound terrain, the Desmophyllum pertusum thicket, a neighbouring mound and the channel between mounds.
facts: NOAA and partners announced this discovery in January 2024 (Sowers et al., Geomatics): a nearly continuous province of cold-water coral mounds stretching about 500 km along the southeastern US coast, covering roughly 6.4 million acres.
Mapping identified 83,908 individual mound-like peak features across the wider province; the tallest known mounds rise up to about 90 m off the seafloor.
The reef-building coral here is Desmophyllum pertusum (formerly Lophelia pertusa), a stony coral that needs no sunlight and instead filters food from the current.
By default you start beside the first objective. With a surface start you begin at the surface directly above a dense mound cluster. Head south-east (about 140°) and descend.
hazards: Total darkness below the top couple hundred metres; only your lights work.
The Gulf Stream runs strong and steady through this area -- expect a persistent current.
Fragile, slow-growing coral: these mounds took thousands of years to build. Keep a respectful distance and do not touch.
Moderate pressure: about 75 atmospheres at 750 m. Your Class B hull is rated to 6,500 m, well within margin.

objectives.title: Survey the dense coral mound cluster
objectives.hint: The dense coral mound cluster is on the Blake Plateau seabed, in the mid-700 m depth range.

objectives.title: Examine a living Desmophyllum pertusum thicket
objectives.hint: A Desmophyllum pertusum thicket lies northeast of the mound cluster, near 770 m.

objectives.title: Chart a neighbouring mound
objectives.hint: A neighbouring mapped mound lies southwest of the main cluster, near 780 m.

objectives.title: Survey the channel between mounds
objectives.hint: The lower channel between mapped mounds is just northwest of the main cluster, near 780 m.
